title: Lee Jae-sang, CEO of Hybe: “2026 Will Be the Year HYBE 2.0 ...
content:
He continued, “The essence of Hybe’s business lies in achieving proactive innovation by merging content and technology based on the core IP of music and artists. Through this, we provide fans with new immersive experiences. This approach lays the foundation for Hybe artists to maintain unique, high-quality, and sustainable IP, regardless of changes in the environment.”

He further emphasized the need to design new experience models based on scarcity. Lee said, “Scarcity is a key factor that can enhance the added value of fandom business and fan experiences. Just as in the past, 2026 will be a crucial year for Hybe to design and test integrated online and offline experience models based on scarcity, driving innovation in the future music fandom business model.” [...] He also presented five key tasks for all members to achieve together this year: verifying the business potential of new ventures and Intellectual Property (IP); establishing the sustainability of IP and expanding the fan base through ‘unexplored innovation’; designing new experience models based on scarcity; securing leadership in the AI-driven prosumer market; and realizing true global governance.

First, Lee stressed the need to prove the validity of proactive investments made in new businesses and artist IP. He explained, “We have already seen significant traffic growth, and now we must shift to generating meaningful revenue to ensure sustainable business. When investments yield results, new investments gain legitimacy and a virtuous cycle of growth is established.” [...] He also highlighted the importance of securing leadership in the prosumer market, where fans and users directly create and share content. Lee stated, “It is necessary to apply integrated and concrete response models from both creative and platform perspectives. By proactively protecting the value of IP and establishing a Fan to Fan model that allows fans to freely create and communicate, we can set the standard for the market.”

Regarding future global strategies, he said, “We will build integrated global governance that organically shares key assets and know-how—such as resources, talent, and content distribution—among global subsidiaries. This will increase cross-border project cases and realize true global synergy.”

Lee Jae-sang, CEO of Hybe. Photo courtesy of Hybe

“If 2025 was a year of ‘investment’ to lay the strategic foundation for HYBE 2.0, then 2026 will mark the beginning of ‘realization’ where those achievements become visible.”

Lee Jae-sang, CEO of Hybe, stated this in his New Year’s address on the 2nd, indicating that this year will be a turning point where the HYBE 2.0 strategy begins to yield tangible results. He noted, “For us, 2025 was a time to strengthen our company’s capacity for sustainable growth through strategic investments and internal consolidation.” He emphasized, “This year, we will demonstrate to the market that our bold, proactive investments were the right choice and that the time spent improving our fundamentals was worthwhile.”

He also presented five key tasks for all members to achieve together this year: verifying the business potential of new ventures and Intellectual Property (IP); establishing the sustainability of IP and expanding the fan base through ‘unexplored innovation’; designing new experience models based on scarcity; securing leadership in the AI-driven prosumer market; and realizing true global governance.

First, Lee stressed the need to prove the validity of proactive investments made in new businesses and artist IP. He explained, “We have already seen significant traffic growth, and now we must shift to generating meaningful revenue to ensure sustainable business. When investments yield results, new investments gain legitimacy and a virtuous cycle of growth is established.”

He continued, “The essence of Hybe’s business lies in achieving proactive innovation by merging content and technology based on the core IP of music and artists. Through this, we provide fans with new immersive experiences. This approach lays the foundation for Hybe artists to maintain unique, high-quality, and sustainable IP, regardless of changes in the environment.”

He further emphasized the need to design new experience models based on scarcity. Lee said, “Scarcity is a key factor that can enhance the added value of fandom business and fan experiences. Just as in the past, 2026 will be a crucial year for Hybe to design and test integrated online and offline experience models based on scarcity, driving innovation in the future music fandom business model.”

He also highlighted the importance of securing leadership in the prosumer market, where fans and users directly create and share content. Lee stated, “It is necessary to apply integrated and concrete response models from both creative and platform perspectives. By proactively protecting the value of IP and establishing a Fan to Fan model that allows fans to freely create and communicate, we can set the standard for the market.”

Regarding future global strategies, he said, “We will build integrated global governance that organically shares key assets and know-how—such as resources, talent, and content distribution—among global subsidiaries. This will increase cross-border project cases and realize true global synergy.”

Finally, Lee concluded, “Hybe’s growth philosophy is clear: to create top-tier IP, lead the fandom business, and expand those achievements into new markets and genres. The protagonists of this journey are all of us. I hope every member of Hybe will become both the driving force and partner in our growth.”

HYBE Bets on “Scarcity” Model to Supercharge BTS 2026 Return
============================================================

HYBE to test if restricted access and premium pricing can turn BTS’ 2026 comeback into a profit engine.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

BY[Diya Mukherjee](https://respawn.outlookindia.com/author/diya-mukherjee)

18 JAN 2026, 11:30 AM

Share![Image 20: share icon](https://mediaassets.outlookindia.com/outlook-respawn/2025-08-18/7et571r2/share-icon.svg)

*   HYBE intends to limit fan access in 2026 in order to experiment with scarcity as a new income driver.
*   The idea will be tested with BTS's much anticipated comeback, which could put strain on its fan economy.
*   Under its "HYBE 2.0" strategy, the company will be prioritizing profitability over mere expansion.

HYBE, the South Korean entertainment company behind global hit BTS, is launching a radical new approach in 2026. As reported by various Korean media sources, CEO Jason Jaesang Lee told employees in a New Year's address that the company may purposely limit fan engagement in the hopes of unlocking new revenue streams. The method, which tests "a new experience model based on scarcity," comes as BTS prepares for its first world tour in nearly four years, giving a high-stakes test for the idea itself.

Lee, who became CEO of HYBE in 2024 after serving as the company’s chief strategist, believes that scarcity may "enhance the added value of the fan experience" through limited-time online and offline products. He reportedly provided few precise examples of the same, like VIP-only events, shortened performance calendars, and restricted access to new releases. However, the basic rationale is clear that supply restrictions could potentially justify higher prices charged by the corporations.

**BTS 2026 Return: A Strategic Catalyst**
-----------------------------------------

All seven members of the band have undergone required South Korean military service in the past four years and are now formally re-entering the world arena with the announcement of 79 tour dates in 34 cities beginning April 9 at Goyang Stadium near Seoul. A fresh album titled _[Arirang](https://respawn.outlookindia.com/pop-culture/pop-culture-news/bts-new-album-2026-arirang-drops-member-specific-vinyls)_, is also scheduled for release on March 20, with its presale window opening from Jan 22 for members of BTS' official fan club named ARMY. A general on-sales will be followed beginning Jan 24 on various platforms, indicating that the scarcity model could be used initially in the comeback period.

BTS' absence reduced its share of HYBE's revenue from almost all of its peak to less than 20% in 2024. Nevertheless, the entertainment giant expanded strongly in the interim, growing into the United States, Latin America, and Africa while launching newer acts such as global girl group [KATSEYE](https://respawn.outlookindia.com/pop-culture/pop-culture-news/katseye-hits-us-top-10-with-186k-sales-in-one-year) in collaboration with Universal Music Group's Geffen Records.

**HYBE 2.0: Profit Over Growth?**
---------------------------------

Lee identified 2026 as the year HYBE must verify its "HYBE 2.0" plan, which involves a shift from a typical label/solution/platform paradigm to a music-platform-tech ecosystem. According to The Asia Business Daily, the HYBE CEO has outlined five priorities which includes, validating new business feasibility, increasing sustainable IP reach, developing the scarcity experience model, securing AI prosumer leadership, and establishing global governance. Additionally, he emphasized on profitability, attributing it as the ultimate measure of success.

In light of this, [HYBE](https://respawn.outlookindia.com/pop-culture/pop-culture-news/hybe-files-rare-global-lawsuit-against-argentine-online-defamer) announced plans to sell around ₩ 5.16 billion (~ $3.5 million USD) of its own shares, reported Music Business Worldwide. The news follows as the company's stock spiked on the event of BTS' homecoming, thus reinforcing market expectations that BTS' return will transform HYBE's top line.

**HYBE Beyond BTS and K-pop**
-----------------------------

HYBE's growth into markets such as India, as well as its efforts to manage global artists like Grammy-winning South African pop diva Tyla, reflect a larger aim to apply its [K-pop](https://respawn.outlookindia.com/pop-culture/pop-culture-news/k-pop-albums-hit-300m-exports-as-home-sales-slide) based playbook globally. That includes Weverse, HYBE's fan engagement platform as well, which has drawn substantial Western artists like Ariana Grande, The Kid LAROI, Gracie Abrams, and Conan Gray, looking for greater revenue than what standard social media channels offer.

Industry analysts will be watching to see if scarcity, which is rarely employed as an intentional fan-economy tool in music, results in long-term profit or alienates the very crowds that HYBE aims to energize. For the time being, the long-awaited reunion of BTS serves as the strategy's first big test.

# Jaesang Lee, CEO of HYBE: "2026 Marks the First Year of 'HYBE 2.0' Results Realization"

by **Lee Yiseul**

**Pubilshed** 02 Jan.2026 10:45(KST)

[**Translate**](//cm.asiae.co.kr/article/2026010210453259652 "Translate") [**Text Size**](javascript:; "Text Size")

### Five Key Focus Areas Announced in New Year's Address

Jaesang Lee, CEO of HYBE. Provided by HYBE

  

Jaesang Lee, CEO of HYBE, declared 2026 as the year of 'realization' in his New Year's address on January 2. He expressed his intention to begin full-scale profit generation, building on the foundation of the 'HYBE 2.0' strategy established last year.

  

CEO Lee emphasized, "If 2025 was a year of investment to lay the groundwork for 'HYBE 2.0,' then 2026 will mark the beginning of visible results. This year, we will prove to the market that our bold investments were the right direction."

  

On this day, Lee announced five key tasks that HYBE must accomplish: ▲Verifying the business potential of new businesses and intellectual property (IP) ▲Establishing the sustainability of IP and expanding the fan base ▲Designing a new experience model based on scarcity ▲Securing leadership in the AI-based prosumer market ▲Implementing true global governance.

  

He identified securing profitability as the top priority. CEO Lee explained, "While we have confirmed significant traffic expansion in new businesses, we must now shift to a phase of generating meaningful profit. A virtuous cycle of investment will be established only when we are confident in sustainable business potential."

  

He further stated, "The essence of HYBE's business is to provide fans with new immersive experiences through the convergence of technology based on core IP. We will lay the groundwork for artists to continue as unique IPs despite changes in the environment."

  

In the fandom business sector, he presented 'scarcity' as the core keyword. CEO Lee said, "Scarcity is an important element that enhances the added value of the fan experience. To innovate future fandom businesses, we will design and test an integrated online and offline experience model based on scarcity."

  

He added, "It is necessary to apply an integrated and concrete response model from both creative and platform perspectives. While preserving the value of IP, we will establish a 'Fan to Fan' model where fans can freely create and communicate, setting a new standard for the market."

  

Regarding global strategy, he emphasized building 'integrated governance' between headquarters and overseas subsidiaries. CEO Lee explained, "We will increase cross-border project cases and realize greater synergy."

  

He concluded, "HYBE's growth philosophy is to create top-level IP, lead the fandom business, and expand into new markets. I ask every member to take ownership of this growth."

[## Music Business Worldwide](https://www.musicbusinessworldwide.com/ "Music Business Worldwide")

# As K-pop superstars BTS return, HYBE CEO to test ‘scarcity’ model for fandom business

By [Daniel Tencer](https://www.musicbusinessworldwide.com/author/dtercer/)

HYBE, the South Korean entertainment giant behind BTS – arguably the world’s biggest K-pop act – is planning to spend 2026 developing “a new experience model based on scarcity,” according to company CEO Jason Jaesang Lee.

“Scarcity is an important element that enhances the added value of the fan experience,” Lee said in a New Year address to HYBE staff, as [reported in media sources](https://cm.asiae.co.kr/en/article/life-general/2026010210453259652) in South Korea.

“To innovate future fandom businesses, we will design and test an integrated online and offline experience model based on scarcity.”

Lee seemingly offered few other details on what the “scarcity” model might look like. Fewer concerts and appearances? VIP-only access to events? Limited access to new releases? But one thing is certain: Increased scarcity drives up prices, and that means potential new revenue growth opportunities.

Whatever HYBE’s plans may be, Lee’s scarcity philosophy is about to be tested with the return of BTS, the global superstar K-pop boy group that has been quite scarce for the past four years as its members completed mandatory military training.

HYBE on Tuesday (January 13) officially [unveiled tour dates](https://www.musicbusinessworldwide.com/bts-world-tour-the-biggest-global-k-pop-tour-of-all-time-to-span-79-shows-across-34-regions/) for BTS’s first world tour in four years, set to begin on April 9 with a three-night engagement at Goyang Stadium near Seoul. The tour will span five continents with **79 shows** in **34 markets**.

That follows last week’s [announcement](https://www.musicbusinessworldwide.com/bts-set-march-album-release-first-world-tour-in-four-years/) that a new BTS album will land on March 20.

In what might be a taste of one element of HYBE’s ‘scarcity’ model, members of BTS’ fan club, ARMY, will have access to a ticket presale for 36 of the shows starting on January 22. Two more Los Angeles shows will be available to ARMY members on January 23. The tour’s general onsale will begin January 24 at LiveNation.com.

With BTS out of the limelight for four years, HYBE has become [less reliant](https://www.musicbusinessworldwide.com/bts-once-hybes-top-earner-accounted-for-below-20-of-the-k-pop-giants-revenues-in-2024-down-from-95-at-their-peak/) on the superstar group for its revenue, and while the BTS boys were busy with their military training, HYBE was busy with major expansions [in the US](https://www.musicbusinessworldwide.com/hybe-launches-us-based-services-arm-with-a-global-focus-and-its-working-with-independent-artists-and-labels/), [Latin America](https://www.musicbusinessworldwide.com/via-the-medellin-music-lab-hybe-latin-america-is-betting-on-colombia-as-a-hotspot-for-global-music-industry-talent/), and [Africa](https://www.musicbusinessworldwide.com/hybe-to-build-a-global-platform-for-african-talent-via-new-partnership-with-tyla-managers-brandon-hixon-and-colin-gayle/).

That has included major investments into the acquisition of local music labels and the establishment of new global musical acts like [**KATSEYE**](https://www.musicbusinessworldwide.com/katseye-named-tiktoks-global-artist-of-the-year-for-2025/) (formed in partnership with **[Universal Music Group](https://www.musicbusinessworldwide.com/companies/universal-music-group/ "Companies > Universal Music Group [4,474 articles]")**‘s **Geffen Records**). In 2026, CEO Lee told HYBE staff, the company aims to turn those investments into profit.

> “To innovate future fandom businesses, we will design and test an integrated online and offline experience model based on scarcity.”
>
> Jason Jaesang Lee, HYBE

It has also meant the development of **Weverse**, HYBE’s platform for superfans that has been [attracting](https://www.musicbusinessworldwide.com/ariana-grande-officially-joins-hybes-weverse-superfan-app1/) Western [artists](https://www.musicbusinessworldwide.com/megan-thee-stallion-joins-weverse-as-hybe-revamps-superfan-platform-to-include-advanced-translation-features-for-artist-posts/) with the promise of a stronger connection with fans and new monetization opportunities.

2026 will be the year HYBE needs to show those investments were worthwhile, Lee told HYBE staff in his address.

“We need to prove the justification for investment in new businesses and artist IP where preemptive investment has been made,” he said, as [quoted by](https://biz.chosun.com/en/en-industry/2026/01/02/4BQSIDXVKZHUXKULDCGH7IZJMM/) *Chosun Daily*.

“We have confirmed meaningful traffic expansion so far, and now we must transition to a phase of valid revenue generation to be confident in sustainable business viability,” Lee said, adding that “when investment shows results, new investment gains legitimacy and a virtuous cycle of growth is established.”

Saying that securing profitability is HYBE’s top priority for 2026, Lee laid out five tasks he says HYBE has to accomplish this year, [per](https://cm.asiae.co.kr/en/article/life-general/2026010210453259652) *Asia Business Daily*:

* verifying the viability of new businesses and IP
* establishing the sustainability of IP and expanding the fan base through “innovation we haven’t tried”
* designing a new experience model based on scarcity
* securing leadership in the AI-based prosumer market
* implementing true global governance

Lee said this marks the “realization” of the plans laid out under the HYBE 2.0 strategy that he [announced](https://www.musicbusinessworldwide.com/hybe-the-home-of-bts-restructures-global-business-as-part-of-new-strategy-called-hybe-2-0/) shortly after being [appointed CEO](https://www.musicbusinessworldwide.com/hybe-ceo-jiwon-park-resigns-chief-strategy-officer-jason-jaesang-lee-named-as-new-chief-exec-at-k-pop-giant12/) in 2024. The mid- and long-term strategy involves shifting the company from its initial “label-solution-platform” structure to a “music-platform-tech” structure.

So far, the “music” part of the new structure has seen, among other things, the reorganization of HYBE’s labels in South Korea and Japan under the new **HYBE Music Group APAC**; the “platform” part has seen the continued expansion of features on the Weverse platform; and the “tech” part has HYBE exploring and investing in new [AI-driven technologies](https://www.musicbusinessworldwide.com/hybes-ai-voice-cloning-company-supertone-unveils-text-to-speech-tool-that-can-create-a-custom-voice-in-just-10-seconds/).

“If 2025 was a year of investment to lay the groundwork for ‘HYBE 2.0,’ then 2026 will mark the beginning of visible results. This year, we will prove to the market that our bold investments were the right direction,” Lee said in his New Year’s address.

---

Yet for fans, the largest change at HYBE this year will no doubt be the return of BTS, a musical phenomenon so strongly linked to HYBE’s fortunes that the company’s stock [plummeted](https://www.musicbusinessworldwide.com/hybe-share-price-plummets-as-bts-announce-break-but-could-bands-hiatus-actually-be-good-news-for-the-korean-company/) when BTS announced their hiatus back in 2022. The stock then [rallied](https://www.musicbusinessworldwide.com/hybe-stock-rallies-to-three-year-high-as-bts-members-complete-military-service/) in the summer of 2025 when BTS members appeared together at HYBE HQ with a “we are back” banner in the background.

Yet, as Lee’s message indicates, the HYBE of today is moving beyond being “the label behind BTS,” and even moving beyond K-pop itself.

“HYBE’s growth philosophy is clear: to create top-tier IP, lead the fandom business, and expand those results into new markets and genres,” Lee said.

In the meantime, the music industry will be watching closely to see just how HYBE’s “scarcity” strategy pans out.Music Business Worldwide

# iM Securities says HYBE will restore operating margin to 10% in 2026

By 

[Park Ji-young](https://biz.chosun.com/en/people/park-jiyoung/)

Published 2025.12.10. 08:46Updated 2025.12.10. 10:13

iM Securities on the 10th said HYBE is expected to restore its operating margin to the 10% range next year. It maintained a "Buy" rating and a target price of 400,000 won, and continued to present it as the top pick in the sector. HYBE's previous day's closing price was 291,000 won.

iM Securities projected HYBE's 2026 operating profit at 514.9 billion won, up 622% from a year earlier, and said the operating margin would recover to the 10% range.

Hwang Ji-won, an analyst at iM Securities, said, "With BTS set to return as a full group next year, the most likely activity schedule now is to release a new album in March and then launch a world tour from April," adding, "We expect to draw about 3.5 million to 4 million attendees, and average ticket prices (ATP) are likely to rise on the back of a higher share of North America and Europe shows and deferred demand."

Announcements on the new album release and world tour are expected early in the year. Considering the scale of the tour to be announced, structural growth in the MD division, strong sales of albums and digital music, and robust online live-streaming revenue, there may be additional upside to earnings.

Hwang said, "Given the leverage effect from the resumption of a large-scale BTS tour and the full-fledged monetization of mid- to lower-tenure artists, including locally localized groups overseas, we recommend continuously increasing positions at the current share-price level."

However, while performance- and MD-based revenue is at an all-time high, operating profit remains weak. In the third quarter of this year, it posted its first quarterly loss since listing. iM Securities said this was due to one-off expenses from restructuring the U.S. subsidiary's business and concentrated investment expenses for new artists.

Hwang said, "In the fourth quarter as well, with remaining expenses related to the U.S. subsidiary and a Latin boy group and game expenses reflected, the short-term improvement in profitability is expected to be limited."

Still, it assessed that the effects of preemptive investment are clear. Hwang said, "Rookie group Cortiz surpassed 1 million in cumulative sales of its debut album, and its monthly listeners on Spotify rank fourth among boy groups, with fandom expansion very steep in key markets," adding, "KATSEYE ranked No. 31 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 4 on the Billboard 200 in its second year since debut and is on its first North American tour."

Given that K-pop groups showing similar metrics can all conduct stadium tours in the United States, next year they are expected to expand to arenas that can accommodate 10,000 to 20,000 people and, as early as then, to domes that can hold more than 30,000.

Hwang said, "Also, given the characteristics of U.S. artists, they are more likely to focus on tour-centered activities, so we can assume more show dates compared with domestic artists."

HYBE plans to debut one team in Korea and one to two teams in the United States next year.
